lesson.title: Quarter, half and three-quarter turns
lesson.subtitle: P4 angle revision
lesson.objective: Connect quarter, half and three-quarter turns to degrees and directions.
lesson.story: A robot faces east and turns clockwise.

steps.title: What fraction of a turn?
steps.prompt: The robot turns clockwise, as the curved arrow shows. What fraction of a full turn is this?
hints: A full turn goes all the way round the circle and back to the start.
Look at how much of the circle the curved arrow covers.
A quarter of the circle is one compass step, like north to east.

steps.title: How many degrees?
steps.prompt: A full turn is 360°. How many degrees is this turn? Enter the number.
hints: A full turn is 360 degrees, and a quarter turn is one quarter of that.
Work out 360 ÷ 4 for one quarter turn.
One quarter turn is 90°. This turn is 1 quarter turn.

steps.title: Where is it facing now?
steps.prompt: Which direction is the robot facing after the turn?
hints: Start from the direction the robot faces now and follow the arrow.
Turn clockwise one quarter turn at a time: north, east, south, west go clockwise.

steps.title: Explain your thinking
steps.prompt: How can you find the degrees in a part of a turn?

choices.label: Count every compass point that you pass as 45°, so a half turn is only 90°.
Take that fraction of 360°: a quarter turn is 90° and a half turn is 180°.
Every part-turn is 90°, whether it is a quarter, a half or a three-quarter turn.

hints: Take a fraction of 360 for each part-turn.
Choose the explanation that starts from 360 degrees.
